statement: Old Babylonian tablets also preserve ritual/incantation practice; such texts show that supernatural or ritual intervention existed alongside mathematical, legal, scribal, and therapeutic practices rather than replacing them.

sources.citation: CDLI P274690 (VS 17, 08), Old Babylonian incantation tablet, ca. 1900–1600 BCE.
sources.author: Cuneiform Digital Library Initiative

sources.citation: CDLI P223455 (TIM 09, 072), Old Babylonian incantation tablet from Shaduppum/Tell Harmal.
sources.author: Cuneiform Digital Library Initiative

notes: This claim records coexistence of ritual explanation/practice with other specialist knowledge. It does not claim ritual explanation was universal or mutually exclusive with empirical treatment.
